title: Secret Leakage in Process Arguments and set -x
platform_conditions: POSIX sh and bash on Linux/macOS; xtrace (set -x/-v) and PS4 expansion are interpreter-level and apply to any CI or interactive context where trace output is captured to logs
security_mechanism: Everything in a command line is world-readable while the process runs: ps, /proc/<pid>/cmdline, and shell/job accounting all expose argv verbatim, so a token passed as 'curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN"' is readable by any local user for the duration of the request. Tracing leaks the same values statically: set -x prints each expanded command line (including the token) to stderr, where CI systems capture it into build logs; PS4 is expanded before printing, and a PS4 containing $(...) executes and emits further data. export propagates a secret to every child process and its environment, which outlives the command in child core dumps and third-party tools; here-docs/here-strings may be implemented via temporary files on disk.

source_sink_clues.source: Credentials the script holds: API tokens, deploy keys, cloud credentials, password variables passed in from CI secret stores or operator prompts.
source_sink_clues.sink: Secrets interpolated into command arguments (curl -H, wget --header, client CLI flags), scripts running with set -x/-v or a PS4 containing command substitution, export of secret variables, and here-doc/here-string bodies carrying credentials

tracking_guards: Check secrets reach the target via stdin, a config file read with fd redirection (curl -K <(...)), or environment variables consumed in-process rather than argv; check no set -x/-v is active on credential-handling paths (and set +x precedes them if tracing is needed); check PS4 contains no $(...) or ${...} expansions; check secrets are not exported beyond the immediate child.
not_candidate_when: The secret is passed via stdin or an fd-based config mechanism that never appears in argv, tracing is disabled and PS4 is a literal constant on all credential paths, or the value in argv is a short-lived, low-privilege identifier rather than a credential (e.g. a public URL or a ticket number).
public_references: CWE-214: Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/214.html
CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/532.html
CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html
